question.problem:
Written in **ascending order**, the solutions to $|5y-1|=6$ are $y=${{field-1}} and $y=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|5y-1|=5y-1,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|5y-1| & =6 \\ 5y-1 & =6 \\ 5y & =7 \\ \frac{5y}{5} & =\frac{7}{5} \\ y & =\frac{7}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|5y-1|=-(5y-1),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|5y-1| & =6 \\ -(5y-1) & =6 \\ -5y+1 & =6 \\ -5y & =5 \\ \frac{-5y}{-5} & =\frac{5}{-5} \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $y=-1$ and $y=\frac{7}{5}.$
